input.quote: 23.4 Customer's Right to Obtain the Source Code. M&I hereby grants to Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable license, through the end of the Term, to use the source code (including the right to make modifications thereto) on the terms and conditions set forth in this Article 23, upon payment of the then current license fees and the occurrence of the following events:
input.rationale: The only licence grant in the Agreement is the Article 23 source code licence (p0310), supported by the use restrictions in Section 23.5 (p0313). Affiliate coverage is better than the fallback: the preamble defines "Customer" to include its Affiliates (p0016), and Section 21.10/21.11 extend Services and future acquisitions to Affiliates, so no notice mechanic is needed and no duplicate affiliate language should be added. The licence is not revocable at M&I's discretion (it is triggered only by the escrow release events and runs through the Term), so this is not walk-away territory. However, the grant is expressly "non-transferable" and Section 23.5(1) separately bars any transfer or assignment to a third party, so the licence would not follow the business to a successor even though Section 22.4 permits assignment of the Agreement in a Customer merger without M&I's consent. That fails the fallback element on transferability to an M&A successor, so we made the minimal conforming edits: the grant is now transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition of Customer, and the Section 23.5(1) prohibition is conformed so it does not contradict that right. We have not pursued the preferred perpetual/irrevocable paid-up terms or express contractor naming (Section 23.5 already permits use by Customer's designee), which are noted rather than redlined.

proposal.summary: Make the source code licence transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position requires the licence to follow the business in an M&A transaction, so we made the Article 23 source code licence transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition of Customer and conformed the Section 23.5 transfer prohibition so it does not contradict that right. Affiliates need no change because the defined "Customer" already includes its Affiliates.
